title: Leaks That Never Stain the Ceiling
description: Water can wet the deck, run along a rafter, and dry before it ever marks the paint. The attic tells on it.
html:
“It does not leak” usually means the bedroom ceiling is clean. That is a low bar. Water enters at a boot or a valley, soaks a few inches of deck, runs downhill on the felt, and dries on the next hot afternoon. The paint never knows. The deck does.

Where the water goes instead

In the attic, look for dark nails, a halo on the decking, or insulation that is packed down in one bay. Those nails rust from the top. By the time a stain shows in the room, the plywood has been wet for seasons. Press the roof from above on a roof inspection and a soft spot tells the same story without a single mark on the ceiling.

Gulf humidity adds a second path. A bath fan dumped into the attic, or a north slope with no intake air, wets the deck from below. That is not a shingle leak, and new shingles will not fix it. We separate the two before we sell you either a repair or a fan duct.

Why this matters before a storm

A deck that is already soft fails a hail inspection differently than a dry one. Tear-off reveals it, and the scope changes. Finding it now means the repair is a section of deck and a boot, not a ceiling, insulation, and a mold conversation.

A simple attic pass

Go up on a dry day with a flashlight. Look at the deck around every pipe you can find, then along the valleys, which often show up as darker plywood in a line. Rust on nail tips means moisture has been at the deck even if the insulation looks fluffy. If you are not comfortable in the attic, that is what the inspection is for. We would rather find it with a light than with a bucket in the hallway.

If the attic smells sweet or the nails look rusty, do not wait for paint damage. Request a free inspection or call (281) 541-0027. We will tell you whether you need roof repair or a longer look at the attic.
